facts.question: Where should skiers go this weekend, and what should they know?
general_advice_topics: check the resort website for lifts and opening
high slopes and north-facing slopes keep snow longest
early-season snow is thin: stay on groomed pistes
read the official avalanche bulletin before off-piste

en.title: Where to ski in the Pyrenees this weekend: Rasos de Peguera, Aramón Cerler and Masella
en.description: Three Pyrenees resorts have snow for the weekend of 7 November. Rasos de Peguera, Aramón Cerler and Masella each hold 17–20 cm on upper slopes after 72 hours of fresh snow.
en.lede: Three resorts stand out for the weekend of 7 November: Rasos de Peguera, Aramón Cerler and Masella. Each has 17 to 20 cm on its upper slopes today, with no more snow forecast before Sunday. This is the best chance to ski while the new snow from the past three days is still there.

p: Rasos de Peguera leads with 20 cm on upper slopes. It received 15 cm of new snow in the last 72 hours, mostly on Tuesday 3 November. Aramón Cerler also holds 20 cm at the top after 7 cm of fresh snow. Masella has 17 cm on its upper runs and got 9 cm in three days.

All three are small resorts where the snow sits mostly above 1,900 m. At lower elevations, the base layer is thin or bare. This means you should aim high and stay on marked runs where the snow is deepest.

The heaviest falls came on Tuesday 3 November: Rasos de Peguera got 12 cm that day, Aramón Cerler 6 cm and Masella 7 cm. Since then the snow has been light—1 cm on Wednesday, 1 cm on Thursday (today). No more snow is in the forecast through Sunday.
This timing matters for your plans. The fresh snow is now three to four days old, so it has begun to settle and bond to what lay beneath. It is still softer than it will be by mid-week.

Watch the freezing level as the weekend progresses. On Saturday 7 November it rises to around 2,850 m at its peak, still above all three resorts' upper runs. By Sunday the freezing level climbs further, reaching 3,130 m in the afternoon.

What this means: rain is unlikely on Saturday at these elevations, but slopes facing south will soften in the sun. Sunday looks clearer and colder at high altitude, though the air is growing warmer. Early morning runs on Sunday will be the most rewarding.

Early November is early. At Rasos de Peguera's mid-mountain height of 1,931 m, today's 5 cm of snow is better than 44 out of the last 46 winters on this date. At Aramón Cerler's mid-mountain (2,060 m), there is no snow depth to measure, but historically there is almost none at this altitude in early November either.
In other words: this is a good weekend by early-season standards. The snow will not last long, so if you plan to visit, go soon.

sections.h: On the ground: what satellite saw
p: At Rasos de Peguera and Aramón Cerler, the latest clear views were older (2 and 31 October respectively), so the snow there is entirely from recent falls. This matters: it confirms the snow is new and has not been sitting around since October.
The drawback is that new, early-season snow is often thin and may hide rocks or grass. Stick to groomed runs and avoid terrain you do not know well.

Before you drive to the mountains, check each resort's website for lift opening times and any closures. Snow depth on the SnowScope map does not mean the resort is running. Many small Pyrenees resorts open later in the season.

Bring layers for a big temperature swing: Saturday morning will be cold at 2,000 m, but midday sun will soften the surface. Sunscreen, goggles and a warmer base layer for the afternoon are essentials. By Sunday the air will be colder but the snow surface may be icy early on, so edges and patience will help more than fresh powder technique.

advice: Start early on Saturday morning to ski the new snow before the sun softens it. Upper slopes and north-facing aspects stay firmest longest.
Check the official avalanche bulletin before any off-piste or touring. Early-season snowpack has weak layers; stability can change quickly with temperature swings.
These resorts' lower runs may be bare or skiable only above 1,800 m. Plan your day around the highest terrain available rather than trying to descend to the base.
Rocks and grass hide under early snow. Stay on marked pistes and runs you know. Ungroomed terrain is riskier now than in deep winter.
No fresh snow is forecast after today, so conditions will get harder and ropier through the week. The weekend is your window.

captions.photo: North-facing slopes high on the Pyrenees hold fresh snow longer in early November. South-facing runs soften quickly as the sun strengthens through the day.

es.title: Dónde esquiar en los Pirineos este fin de semana: Rasos de Peguera, Aramón Cerler y Masella
es.description: Combinamos el espesor de nieve de hoy, la nieve nueva de las últimas 72 horas y la previsión para elegir Rasos de Peguera, Aramón Cerler y Masella. …
es.lede: Combinamos el espesor de nieve de hoy, la nieve nueva de las últimas 72 horas y la previsión para elegir Rasos de Peguera, Aramón Cerler y Masella. De estas estaciones, Rasos de Peguera tiene hoy más nieve en las pistas altas, unos 20 cm; después vienen Aramón Cerler 20 cm y Masella 17 cm.

p: Rasos de Peguera recibió 15 cm de nieve nueva en las últimas 72 horas. En su último día despejado, el 2 de noviembre, los satélites no vieron nieve en Rasos de Peguera: quizá solo está en lo más alto o cayó después.

Aramón Cerler recibió 7 cm de nieve nueva en las últimas 72 horas. En su último día despejado, el 31 de octubre, los satélites no vieron nieve en Aramón Cerler: quizá solo está en lo más alto o cayó después.
Masella recibió 9 cm de nieve nueva en las últimas 72 horas. Los satélites vieron Masella cubierta de nieve el 4 de noviembre, su último día despejado.

sections.h: Altitud, laderas y cota de nieve
p: En Rasos de Peguera, la cota de congelación llega a 2970 m-3520 m el 8 de noviembre, por encima de la cota alta de la estación (2036 m): ese día puede haber lluvia o nieve húmeda en todas las pistas.
Busca la nieve en lo alto y en las laderas orientadas al norte: la guardan más tiempo; las orientadas al sur la pierden antes.
Antes de salir fuera de pista o de travesía, lee el boletín oficial de aludes (enlaces abajo).
Las previsiones a varios días pueden cambiar: vuelve a mirar el mapa el día antes de viajar.

advice: Nieve en el mapa no significa que la estación esté abierta: consulta remontes y fechas de apertura en su web.
Las estaciones pequeñas cerca de las líderes suelen tener la misma nieve con menos gente: compáralas en el mapa.
La nieve de principio de temporada es fina. Quédate en pistas abiertas y pisadas: piedras y hierba están justo debajo.
Busca la nieve en lo alto y en las laderas orientadas al norte: la guardan más tiempo; las orientadas al sur la pierden antes.
Activa una alerta de nieve polvo en la app SnowScope para saber cuándo Rasos de Peguera recibe nieve nueva.
